Clear cell sarcoma of the scapula: Immunohistochemical stains: positive for tumor markers S-100 protein, HMB-45, NSE, EMA, cytokeratins, and myosin
CT scans and MRI images: soft tissue mass 45 × 45 mm localized in the lower scapular region between infraspinatus and teres minor muscles with bone invasion of the lower part of the scapula
Areas of necrosis and hemorrhage and tumor spreading into the surrounding muscles and scapula
Large rounded cells had pleomorphic nuclei and large amounts of clear cytoplasm
Spindle-shaped cells had palely staining eosinophilic cytoplasm
Open biopsy specimen: rubbery, homogenous, white tissue with no attachment to the skin

top_diagnoses.diagnosis: Clear cell sarcoma of the scapula
top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The presence of a painful mass, restricted movement, osteolytic lesion, and positive bone scan, along with positive immunohistochemical stains for S-100 protein and other tumor markers, strongly support this diagnosis.
The presence of a mass, osteolytic lesion, and positive bone scan, along with variable immunohistochemistry, provide some support for this diagnosis, but it is less likely than clear cell sarcoma.
The presence of a mass, osteolytic lesion, and positive bone scan, along with MDM2 positivity, provide some support for this diagnosis, but it is less likely than clear cell sarcoma.
The presence of a mass, osteolytic lesion, and positive bone scan, along with clear cell morphology, provide some support for this diagnosis, but it is less likely than clear cell sarcoma.
The presence of an osteolytic lesion and positive bone scan, along with osteoid production, provide some support for this diagnosis, but it is less likely than clear cell sarcoma.
